text: The B.S. in Computer Science degree plan (2026-2027) requires 124 hours (45 in residence, last semester at UTD) with a minimum 2.0 cumulative and major GPA. A grade of C or better is required for Major Requirements and Prerequisites. The plan consists of: Major Introductory Courses (1 hour); Major Preparatory Requirements (39 hours, counted in the major GPA); Major Core Requirements (39 hours, major GPA); Technical Electives (9 hours, major GPA); Remaining State Core Curriculum (24 hours); and Free Electives (13 hours).
source_title: B.S. in Computer Science Degree Plan (2026-2027)

text: Major Introductory Courses for the B.S. in Computer Science (2026-2027), for first year in college only (transfer students see advisor): ECS 1100 Intro to Engineering and CS [First Year Only] (1 hour). Major Preparatory Requirements (lower division, major GPA, 39 hours): ECS 1210 Foundations of Engineering and Computer Science I (2); MATH 2413 Differential Calculus or MATH 2417 Calculus I (4); CS 1436 Programming Fundamentals (4); MATH 2414 Integral Calculus or MATH 2419 Calculus II (4); CS 1337 Computer Science I (3); PHYS 2325 Mechanics (3); PHYS 2125 Physics Laboratory I (1); CS 2305 Discrete Mathematics for Computing I (3); CS 2336 or CS 2337 Computer Science II (3); CS 2340 Computer Architecture (3); PHYS 2326 Electromagnetism and Waves (3); PHYS 2126 Physics Laboratory II (1); and MATH 2418 Linear Algebra (4).
source_title: B.S. in Computer Science Degree Plan (2026-2027)
section_heading: Major Introductory Courses and Major Preparatory Requirements

text: Major Core Requirements for the B.S. in Computer Science (2026-2027) (upper division, major GPA, 39 hours): CS 3341 Probability & Statistics in CS/SE (3); CS 3345 Data Structures & Intro to Algorithmic Analysis (3); CS 3377 C/C++ Programming in a UNIX Envirn (3); ECS 2390 Professional & Technical Communication (3); CS 3354 Software Engineering (3); CS 4337 Programming Language Paradigms (3); CS 4341 Digital Logic and Computer Design (3); CS 4141 Digital Systems Laboratory (1); CS 3162 Professional Responsibility in CS/SE (1); CS 4348 Operating Systems Concepts (3); CS 4349 Adv Algorithm Design & Analysis (3); CS 4384 Automata Theory (3); CS 4347 Database Systems (3); and CS 4485 Computer Science Project (4).
source_title: B.S. in Computer Science Degree Plan (2026-2027)

text: Technical Electives for the B.S. in Computer Science (2026-2027) (major GPA, 9 hours): three CS Technical Electives at the CS 4XXX level (3 hours each). Remaining State Core Curriculum (lower division, 24 hours; see advisor for grade requirement): RHET 1302 Communication (Core: 010) (3); GOVT 2305 Government/Political Science (Core: 070) (3); GOVT 2306 Government/Political Science (Core: 070) (3); two American History (Core: 060) courses (3 each); Language, Philosophy and Culture (Core: 040) (3); Creative Arts (Core: 050) (3); and Social Behavioral Science (Core: 080) (3). Free Electives (13 hours): four 3-hour Free Electives and one 1-hour Free Elective. The plan assumes a 15 credit hour average per long semester.
